acceptanceCriteria.statement: Phase 0 ground truth: a plain answer to 'what actually costs 3 s' on entering PRISM, and whether option D's 7.8125 pc slab can stay under 50 ms (plan §8).

verifyVia.input: In the browser, warp to XIGMAG-2AE101G (IOTA AQUILA-6, near the core) and to Sol; enter PRISM in design 1 with and without the profiler; record query bounds, loop and density-call counts, per-callback times, both nav instances; run the option-D slab benchmark at the inner galaxy and Sol in the same browser.
verifyVia.observable: A written report (docs/WORKSTREAMS/naming-prism-segments-2026-10-02/PHASE0.md) naming the dominant cost with numbers, explaining the browser-vs-headless gap (3 s vs 0.2 s), and stating the measured option-D slab time at both locations against 50 ms.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: MEASURED LIVE 2026-10-02 at 7554b70 (Chrome 154, lane-A server :5175), report PHASE0.md, Astra second opinion folded in (PHASE0 §10). What costs the 3 s: the per-cell galaxy-density call, 62% of CPU in _spiralPotentialOnly (GalacticMap.js:844, 7 calls x 6 arms per cell). XIGMAG is at R = 17.0 kpc (the sparse rim, not near the core as this AC says), so its query box is 76.8 pc wide because _localCubeSize is used as a half-width (NavComputer.js:1188 -> :3698/:3750 vs :1593): 728,424 cells per 100 pc step vs Sol's 64,792, 1.86-2.18 s per query, 3.5-4.2 s per background callback, 32 callbacks, 116.6 s to fill the column (63,924 rows). Browser vs headless: the headless probes never tested R = 17; on identical bounds node takes 1.28-1.33 s and Chrome 2.0 s (same stars, same density calls), so the gap is ~10x box size times an observed ~1.5-1.65x engine factor; the profiler added nothing measurable. The cockpit nav keeps loading its own column alongside the overlay. Option D slab (7.8125 x 7.8125 x 100 pc) in Chrome: warm query 26.5-30.8 ms (max 32.1) inner galaxy, 29.2-30.9 ms (max 33.0) Sol, 22.6-26.5 ms XIGMAG, 4.0-4.4 ms bulge - all under 50 ms; with a cold feature cache 66-71 ms inner and 55 ms Sol - over 50 ms. Naming (~2 us/star) and multiplicity (~18-21 ms per dense slab, inferred) come on top. Verdict: Decision 0 stands, conditional on the Phase 3 loader slicing inside a slab under one deadline shared by both nav instances. Not yet measured (Phase 3): leaving PRISM, the six sort modes, cancelling a slab, swapping a same-size slab. Status sha note: 7554b70 is the code that was measured; the report lands in the commit after it, which cannot cite its own sha (no amend).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every procedural star has exactly one owner — one box at each level (half-open: lower edge in, upper edge out, on every axis, y = 0 is N1) and one (tier, cell) identity — fixed by the exact grid constants (2 kpc sectors, 16×16 regions, 16×16 prisms of 7.8125 pc, offset 1.00390625 kpc, 100 pc slabs, row 1 at the top).

verifyVia.input: Unit tests over the grid module and HashGridStarfield: stars on faces, edges and corners, negative coordinates, y = 0, coarse tiers, equal seeds; round trip address → bounds → address; injectivity over a sampled volume.
verifyVia.observable: Every case resolves to exactly one address and one identity; Sol resolves to sector N10 and the galactic centre to J10; sabotaging the half-open rule (closed upper edge) turns the face/corner tests red.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: HEADLESS, built 5b9ba76 + Astra fixup 12e1f05 (2026-10-02). src/generation/GalaxyGrid.js holds the frozen grid (2 kpc sectors, 16x16 regions, 16x16 prisms of 7.8125 pc, offset 1.00390625 kpc, 100 pc slabs, row 1 at the top) and one half-open addressOf/boundsOf for every level; HashGridStarfield stamps every star with ident = its generating (tier, cell), carried from the loop that made it, and key 'p:<tier>:<cx>:<cy>:<cz>'. Tests: GalaxyGrid.test.js (21) - faces, edges, corners, negatives, y = 0 is N1, round trip, injectivity over a sampled volume, Sol = N10, the centre = J10, and 'numbers every cell that can place a star in the box - and ONLY those' + 'a cell whose lowest star sits exactly on the excluded upper face is not a candidate' (Astra finding 4: slotOf now uses the generator's own placement arithmetic, 12 slots in Sol's N1 prism at 0.05 kpc, not 16); HashGridStarfield.identity.test.js (14) - every query and the sky carry the generating slot, endpoint stars included, and a 7-case fixture proves generation output byte-unchanged. Sabotage-checked: a closed upper edge turns the face/corner tests red; putting a tolerance back on the slot's upper face turns both slot tests red. Not in this AC (later phases): the live queries still accept both edges of their box, so one star can appear in two query results (same key, same owner) - the Phase 3 loader must filter by owner; and GalacticMap.hashCombine loses bits (a float multiply before |0), which is why same-seed stars exist - it stays unchanged here because fixing it would change which stars exist, and whether it is frozen with the names must be decided before Phase 4/5.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The nav finds stars by that identity, not by the 32-bit seed — two stars with the same seed can no longer be clicked, selected, de-duplicated or warped to as each other (index.js:496, picking.js:271, state.js:571/611/1031, NavComputer.js:3755). Debug / title / ?system= systems are named from their own seed, outside the galaxy-name guarantee.

verifyVia.input: Headless driver test: inject two stars with equal seeds into one slab; click each row and each map mark; warp from each.
verifyVia.observable: Each click selects its own star and each warp resolves to its own position; reverting any one lookup to the seed makes the test fail.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: HEADLESS, built 88c3d98 + Astra fixup 12e1f05 (2026-10-02). Every nav lookup goes through starIdentity.js: sameStar (star keys decide; a 'k:' KnownSystems system against a row, or a record with no key, falls back to 0.1 pc) and findStar (the NEAREST same-star row, never the first inside 0.1 pc - distinct stars sit 0.023 pc apart). Fixup closed Astra's findings 1-3 and 5: the sky-target keep (main.js dispatchNavAction) and _tryAutoSelectExternalTarget compare keys, and a keyed target whose row is not loaded keeps the selection instead of taking a neighbour; catalogue sky stars, search hits ('r:' / 'k:'), KnownSystems arrivals ('k:<name>'), the external target, the driver's commit and the autopilot all carry the key; the real-star merge de-duplicates by catalogue key, not name. Tests: navStarIdentity.test.js (30) incl. 'click -> commit -> dispatch -> ARRIVAL -> reopen: each twin lands on itself' - two stars with one seed, rail and bars, map mark and list row, each of: no warp in flight, a sky target 0.03 pc away, pre-FOLD overwrite, post-FOLD redirect, through the real main.js dispatchNavAction, _consumePendingPlayerWarp and _arriveAtWarpTargetStar (lifted out of the FOLD and reveal functions unchanged so they can run headless) and the nav's own openToCurrentSystem; plus the sky-neighbour, unloaded-keyed-target, search-hit and autopilot cases; NavComputer.realStarKey.test.js (4) incl. two same-name catalogue records in one load, both orders, reload. 11 sabotages (each lookup reverted to position/first-match/name, each key dropped) all turn a test red. Visible change, required by this AC's de-dup clause: once Sol's column is fully loaded 5 more procedural stars appear (9,988 -> 9,993, all 0.6-2.9 kpc off the plane), and with the catalogue on a second 'p Eridani' row appears from the first load (the binary's other HYG record, 18.4 pc vs 18.7 pc, replacing a procedural star within 2 pc); debug / ?system= / dev-tools systems are named 'SEED <seed>'. Every other headless frame (GALAXY, SECTOR, REGION, SYSTEM, both designs, list, legacy) is byte-identical to 88c3d98. Not live-verified in a browser.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "each cell in the galaxy should represent a single sector … every cell in the sector view should be displaying a single region … every cell in the region view should be displaying a single prism" — in designs 1 and 2 (made in nav-240p-lab.html and extracted), with edge labels on every grid; PRISM is one fixed 7.8125 pc column (WASD stops at its edge, zoom can pull back past it). Legacy grids kept correct.

verifyVia.input: Live, in both designs: click cells at GALAXY, SECTOR and REGION (centre, edge, corner cells; Sol; the core); drag the map then click again; read the edge labels.
verifyVia.observable: GALAXY draws 19×19 cells and each drawn cell's bounds equal exactly one sector's; SECTOR and REGION draw 16×16 world-locked cells; every click drills to exactly the clicked cell's bounds (published S.mapProj / drill target compared numerically); after a drag the same world point is under the same cell id; every row and column carries an edge label.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The autopilot drills through the same cells the pilot would — its private 8×8 / 44 kpc grid (AutopilotNavSequence.js:464-473) is replaced by the shared address → view and enter-column functions.

verifyVia.input: Run the autopilot's nav drill sequence to a destination; separately drill manually to the same destination.
verifyVia.observable: The sequence of cells the autopilot shows at each level equals the manual drill's cell ids exactly; the hover highlight and the animation use the same grid.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "Here" is worked out from the player's own position, independent of the rows being browsed; a column that is not the player's shows no here-mark (state.js:1018-1027).

verifyVia.input: Live: open PRISM on the player's own column, then on a neighbouring column; repeat in a system with no loaded row for the player.
verifyVia.observable: Own column: the here-mark sits on the player's star and the label names the current system; other column: no here-mark, and the where-am-I label still names the current system (never the nearest browsed row).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "The update build for the prism nav view needs to include performance optimization" — PRISM loads one 100 pc slab at a time with a deadline-based, resumable, cancellable loader that also budgets naming, merge, sort and publish. No main-thread task over 50 ms. Option D is confirmed here or reopened before any name is frozen.

verifyVia.input: Live, in both designs and both nav instances: enter PRISM, browse slabs, change every sort mode, jump with the segment bar, leave mid-load (cancel), re-enter cold — at XIGMAG-2AE101G (core) and at Sol; record a performance trace for each.
verifyVia.observable: No main-thread task longer than 50 ms in any trace (long-task list empty above 50 ms); keys pressed during loading act within one frame of being pressed (no queued burst).

acceptanceCriteria.maxRuling2026-10-02: "let's try to make the system work without this, but if needed we can come up with some kind of aesthetic-appropriate 'scanning' screen for loading windows" — target: NO loading screen (sliced loader keeps every task < 50 ms and the view live). Fallback only if that cannot be met: a 4th-gen-menu-style 'SCANNING' screen/overlay for the load window (see memory well-dipper-aesthetic-generations); it does not relax the 50 ms main-thread rule.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "you could see the un-highlighted segments in the nav bar and click or drag to a new one quickly, or use existing R and F controls to slowly pan up or down" — a 60-cell segment bar (N30…N1, S1…S30, coloured thin / thick / halo at 0.3 / 1.0 kpc) beside the fine gauge in design 1 and in design 2 (incl. list mode; minimap moved left); the fine ±2 pc gauge follows the view, ship shown as an edge mark when out of range.

verifyVia.input: Live: on PRISM click a far segment (mid-plane to N20), drag along the bar, press R/F, grab the fine gauge after a jump.
verifyVia.observable: One click moves the view to the clicked slab (camera y within that slab's bounds) and highlights its cell; dragging steps slab by slab; R/F move continuously within the slab as today; grabbing the fine gauge after a jump does NOT throw the view back to the ship's height; the bar never overlaps design 2's minimap (no shared texels).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Which procedural star a real catalogue star replaces is decided over a full 3D neighbourhood by identity, so the result is the same whatever slab loads first (NavComputer.js:3779-3815).

verifyVia.input: Headless: load the same column's slabs in three different orders, including a real star within 2 pc of a column or slab edge.
verifyVia.observable: The set of replaced procedural identities and resulting rows is identical across all orders.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Max approves the vocabulary: 361 sector words (crisp in the core, soft on the rim) and samples from two separate 256-syllable sets; all 65,536 column words screened exhaustively against real names, constellations and profanity.

verifyVia.input: An Artifact review page (one medium) listing every sector word on its grid position and column-word samples, with Passes / Needs a fix + notes autosaved to its db.
verifyVia.observable: Max's verdicts read back from the db; every rejected word replaced and re-reviewed; the exhaustive screen report shows zero hits.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "naming stars … based on their galactic location" with "readable syllabes at the beginning": every procedural star's name spells its address, e.g. 'Thessa Korabi N1 M-955'; real, catalogue, KnownSystems and fictional names untouched; still unique by construction, disjoint from every name shape whose lookup joins contents (real-star overlay, KnownSystems aliases), and the same on every visit.

verifyVia.input: Unit tests: name a sampled grid of procedural identities; name every catalogue / real / KnownSystems entry; re-name the same identity via each call site; build-time lookup-key check.
verifyVia.observable: Zero duplicate procedural names; zero procedural names equal to any catalogue, real, archive-host or KnownSystems name or alias; every call site returns the identical string; real names byte-identical to before.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The name on a nav row is the name you arrive at — rows, previews, warp arrival, teleports and the self-warp guard all use the one namer (teleports through the shared arrival resolver).

verifyVia.input: Live: warp from a PRISM row, from search, from the map, and by teleport; at each arrival open the nav.
verifyVia.observable: The arrival system name equals the row's name exactly; the where-am-I label and the 'no warp to here' guard recognise the current system in every case.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "the label … doesn't give me all the information … it's not color-coded to match the highlight that shows me visually where I am" — the where-am-I label shows the full address, each part in the colour of its highlighted cell on the map.

verifyVia.input: Live: at each level in both designs, read the label and the highlighted cells.
verifyVia.observable: The label's parts name the current system, sector, region and column; each part's ink equals the ink of the matching highlighted cell (one shared resolver for text and highlight).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The whole: I can navigate the galaxy coherently — every cell is one place, I can read where I am and where I'm going, the prism is quick to move through, and names tell me where a star is.

verifyVia.input: Max walks the nav in both designs, from Sol and from the core, using the segment bar, warping and arriving.
